## Verdict

**Dorado** costs least for a team of 18, at **$162 per month**. It is the only vendor whose seat minimum (10) falls below the team size, so all 18 seats are billed at the list rate with nothing wasted. Inkwell bills for 25 seats and Borealis for 50, pushing their effective cost well above their headline rates.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $9 | 10 |
| Inkwell | $14 | 25 |
| Borealis | $19 | 50 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 18 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Dorado:** minimum 10 < 18, so 18 seats paid. 18 × $9 = **$162 per month**. Effective rate $9.00 per person.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 25 > 18, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $14 = **$350 per month**. Seven unused seats, worth $98. Effective rate $19.44 per person ($350 ÷ 18).
- **Borealis:** minimum 50 > 18, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $19 = **$950 per month**. Thirty-two unused seats, worth $608. Effective rate $52.78 per person ($950 ÷ 18).

Dorado is $188 per month cheaper than Inkwell and $788 per month cheaper than Borealis — $2,256 and $9,456 over twelve months.

## Risks

Seat minimums, not per-seat rates, drive this result, so the ranking is sensitive to headcount. Inkwell's unused-seat penalty disappears at 25 people, where it costs $350 against Dorado's $225; Borealis reaches list rate only at 50 seats, where it costs $950 against Dorado's $450. Dorado holds the lowest per-seat rate at every size on this list, so growth does not reorder the result. Shrinking below 10 people leaves Dorado billing a $90 floor.

This compares list price only. The price list carries no information on features, support tiers, usage limits or security posture, so a cheaper seat may buy less product. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual commitments, negotiated discounts, onboarding and migration costs are not in the source and could change the totals.
